oracle: projects/xml/cpp/cxxtools/oracle.py (Python expat without namespace processing, ordered attributes)
output_name_form: raw qualified names (prefix:local); xmlns/xmlns:* are ordinary attributes
api: cxxtools::xml::XmlReader(std::istream&) over a std::istringstream of the local bytes; XmlReader::get() then next() until Node::EndDocument; StartElement::name() and attributes() (Attribute::name()/value()), Characters::content(); cxxtools::String converted with Utf8Codec::encode
namespace_semantics: cxxtools 3.0.0's XmlReader reports element and attribute names as written and keeps xmlns/xmlns:* declarations as ordinary attributes in source order. StartElement has a NamespaceContext and namespaceUri(prefix), but xmlreader.cpp never fills it, so no URI is available; the adapter resolves nothing.
coverage: LLVM source coverage of the static libcxxtools built from Debian's orig tarball (no SSL, demos or unit tests); XmlReader is in src/xml/xmlreader.cpp
coverage_limit: Two valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 controls without DOCTYPE establish cxxtools XmlReader's element, attribute, comment, processing-instruction, CDATA and character events for them only, as a raw-name path: qualified names, xmlns attributes, attribute order and decoded values, depth and trimmed text runs. No namespace URI, expanded name or in-scope binding is reported. Coverage counts every libcxxtools line reached (string, codec and stream helpers included); the XML reader's own lines are reported separately. DTDs, entities beyond the controls' references, other encodings, XML 1.1 and well-formedness rejection are not established. The expected outputs come from oracle.py (Python pyexpat in non-namespace mode, a different family from cxxtools).
